indicatorNotes.switched: the letters of HER SHOES are switched around into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone swapped a fashion model's shoes as a prank, and she is not amused.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a clothes-horse is not literally a model but someone who lives to show off clothes, which is what a model does.
annotation.definitionFit: A clothes-horse is a person devoted to wearing fashionable clothes, much like a model.

entries.clue: Rogue's heading off to pitch a tent (4)

indicatorNotes.heading off: the heading, or first letter, of the word is taken off

blocks.note: SCAMP (a rogue) without its first letter S

annotation.surface: A rascal sets off on a camping trip.
annotation.walkthrough: Read "Rogue's" as "the rogue has": SCAMP has its heading taken off.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: campers camp by pitching a tent for the night.

indicatorNotes.outing: an outing takes LIMA out of its usual shape

annotation.surface: Picking a trip to Lima, Peru, is the best choice.
annotation.walkthrough: Lima looks like a destination for an outing, but it is just four letters to shake up.
annotation.definitionFit: Optimal means best or most favourable.

blocks.note: H is Hotel in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: Someone trails a fish all the way to a hotel.
annotation.walkthrough: "Fish to hotel" means the fish is added to the hotel, so H comes first.
annotation.definitionFit: To heel is to follow closely behind, as a dog does.

indicatorNotes.Mis: the prefix mis- means wrongly, so ALIGNS is arranged wrongly

blocks.note: anagram fodder ALIGNS, 6 letters, after the prefix Mis

annotation.walkthrough: The one word splits in two: "mis" is the instruction and "aligns" the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a signal, like a nod or a light, is an indication of something.

entries.clue: Late time for the bowler to appear? (7)

blocks.note: in cricket an over is a bowler's set of six balls

annotation.surface: A cricket bowler is late turning up for his spell.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket each bowler delivers an over of six balls in turn, so an over is his time. The question mark flags the reading of the whole phrase as "over due".
annotation.definitionFit: Overdue means late, past the expected time.

indicatorNotes.scamper: the rats scamper about, scattering their letters
indicatorNotes.around: the jumbled RATS goes around Y

annotation.surface: Rats run around a god, and someone confirms it.
annotation.walkthrough: "Yes, deity" reads like an exclamation, but the yes is only its initial letter, which the scrambled rats wrap around.
annotation.definitionFit: A satyr is a minor woodland deity of Greek myth, half man and half goat.

entries.clue: Wait up with the French items of food (7)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top

annotation.surface: Someone stays awake late with some French dishes.
annotation.walkthrough: "Wait up" looks like staying up late; here "up" turns BIDE over.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the noun edibles covers anything fit to eat, so items of food.

entries.clue: Religious hat back in another time (5)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer sits inside the words that follow

annotation.surface: A bishop's hat is coming back into fashion some other day.
annotation.walkthrough: The letters straddle the gap between the two words and read right to left.
annotation.definitionFit: A mitre is the tall pointed hat worn by bishops.

indicatorNotes.about: GREED goes about, or around, ET

annotation.surface: A film about gluttony gets a warm reception.
annotation.walkthrough: "About" reads as "on the subject of", as in a film about greed, but here it means around.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the past tense: guests who were greeted at the door were welcomed.

entries.clue: Grandma's bash unfortunately brings sort of raid (5,3,4)

indicatorNotes.unfortunately: things go wrong for the letters, which end up out of order

annotation.surface: Grandma's party goes badly wrong when it is raided.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is ignored; only the letters of GRANDMAS BASH count.
annotation.definitionFit: A smash-and-grab is a raid where a window is broken and goods snatched.

entries.clue: Have they escaped from awful regimes? (7)

annotation.definition: Have they escaped from awful regimes?

indicatorNotes.awful: the letters of REGIMES are put into an awful state

annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: emigres are people who fled their country, often a harsh regime.
annotation.definitionFit: Emigres are people who have left their country, often for political reasons.

indicatorNotes.during: the boy comes during, or inside, the month

annotation.surface: A boy falls ill at some point in the month.
annotation.walkthrough: "During" is a time word that suits the month, but here it means inside: the boy sits within it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: malady is a slightly old-fashioned word for an illness or ailment.

annotation.definitionNote: the first sense is the verb drop off; the second is the noun drop-off

blocks.note: a phrasal verb for nodding off
a noun for the place where passengers or goods are set down

annotation.surface: Someone dozes off at a delivery bay.
annotation.walkthrough: The spoken phrase and the hyphenated noun share their letters, which is what lets one answer serve both halves.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses of one phrase: dozing is dropping off, and a drop-off is a place where people or goods are let out.

entries.clue: Pounding tool and stone carried by footballer (6)

indicatorNotes.carried by: the stone is carried inside the footballer's name

blocks.note: ST is short for stone, the British weight

annotation.surface: A footballer lugs around a hammer and a rock.
annotation.walkthrough: A stone is a British weight of 14 pounds, abbreviated ST.
annotation.definitionFit: A pestle is the tool used to pound things in a mortar.

entries.clue: A vanquished leader during route finding hard work (7)

indicatorNotes.leader: the leader of vanquished is its first letter
indicatorNotes.during: A and V go during, or inside, the route

annotation.surface: A defeated leader hits hard going on the campaign trail.
annotation.walkthrough: "Vanquished leader" looks like a beaten politician, but it only gives V.
annotation.definitionFit: Travail is painful or laborious effort.

indicatorNotes.converts: SPRITE is converted into a new arrangement

annotation.surface: A clergyman wins a fairy over to the faith.
annotation.walkthrough: "Converts" fits the religious surface, but it is the letters that get converted.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: minister is a general word for a member of the clergy, and a priest is one.

entries.clue: Chef wanted damson or Gary gets upset (6,6)

indicatorNotes.gets upset: the letters are upset, knocked out of order

annotation.surface: A chef asked for a damson, or else Gary gets angry.
annotation.walkthrough: Gordon Ramsay is a famous British TV chef known for his temper, which the surface plays on.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Gordon Ramsay is a famous British TV chef, one instance of a chef.

blocks.note: of steak: less cooked and redder inside

annotation.surface: Something gets bloodier but happens less often.
annotation.walkthrough: "Bloodier" suggests violence, but it is the steak sense of rare.
annotation.definitionFit: Rarer steak is bloodier, and rarer events happen less often.

entries.clue: Othello to accept Ford model car (5)

indicatorNotes.to accept: MOOR accepts T into its middle

blocks.note: Othello is Shakespeare's Moor of Venice

annotation.surface: Othello agrees to take a Ford as his car.
annotation.walkthrough: The Model T was Henry Ford's famous early car.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal British use: motor is a colloquial name for a car, as in motorist.

indicatorNotes.sound of: we want the sound of the word, not its spelling

blocks.note: a tease is a person who mocks

annotation.surface: Someone jeers at the babbling of a river.
annotation.walkthrough: The Tees is a river in north-east England.
annotation.definitionFit: The Tees is an English river flowing into the North Sea.

blocks.note: OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, an honour after a name

annotation.surface: Someone hauls a nobleman off to receive his title.
annotation.walkthrough: "Lug" looks like the verb to haul, but it is British slang for an ear. The OBE is a British honour.
annotation.definitionFit: Lug is informal British for an ear, and the lobe is its soft lower part.

indicatorNotes.nameless: nameless means lacking a name, and N is the abbreviation for name, so TRANCE loses its N

annotation.surface: Just a hint of an unknown daze.
annotation.walkthrough: N is the standard abbreviation for name.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a scintilla is the smallest particle, and a trace is a tiny amount.

indicatorNotes.cooked: OR ELSE is cooked, mixed into a new order

blocks.note: returns on an investment are its profit

annotation.surface: A threat: the pudding had better come back cooked, or else!
annotation.walkthrough: "Returns" looks like a reversal instruction, but it is a plain noun meaning profit.
annotation.definitionFit: Profiteroles are choux-pastry balls filled with cream, served as a dessert.
